summary: Suffolk County DA and county judge; John's 5th cousin 6x removed; his heirs held the blunderbuss 'Old Crib' in 1898.
bio:
Path: Bull Smith → Richard 2d → Sarah (m. Nathaniel Woodhull) → Gen. Nathaniel Woodhull → Elizabeth (m. Henry Nicoll) → Eliza Willett Nicoll (m. Richard Smith) → J. Lawrence. His Smith surname also comes through his father's own Smithtown line.

A closer route than the 5C6R on the site. Pelletreau ([R4-S2]) gives his father as Richard Smith 5th (1770-1831), son of Richard 4th (d. 1811), son of Ebenezer Smith and Anna, daughter of Job Smith 2d, son of Job Smith 1st, John's 10th-great-grandfather. Path: Job 1st -> Job 2d -> Anna -> Richard 4th -> Richard 5th -> J. Lawrence, 5 generations: 4th cousin 6 times removed (also 4C7R via Bull Smith -> Richard 2d -> Ebenezer, and 5C6R via his mother Eliza Nicoll -> Gen. Nathaniel Woodhull). Princeton 1837; Assembly 1846; Suffolk DA 1850; county judge 1858 ([R4-S1]). Wikipedia ([R4-S3]) adds that his wife Sarah Nicoll Clinch was the niece and adopted daughter of the merchant A. T. Stewart, and that he was perhaps the county's largest landowner. Children: Cornelia (Mrs Prescott Hall Butler), Louise Nicoll (Mrs Frank Sayre Osborne), Kate Annette (Mrs J. Bloomfield Wetherill), Bessie Springs (Mrs Stanford White), Ella Batavia (Mrs Devereux Emmet) and James Clinch.
